 Oral Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment & award dated 20.01.2020 passed in MVC No.383/2018 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & AMACT., Bailhongal (for short, 'Tribunal').
3. Heard.
4.

Learned counsel Sri.Hanamanth R.Latur appearing for the appellant-claimant would submit that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income, disability and awarded meager compensation on all other heads.
Thus, he seeks for reassessment of the compensation amount appropriately by allowing the appeal.

5. Per contra, learned counsel Sri.S.C.Bhuti appearing for the respondent-Corporation supporting the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal submits that in the absence of cogent and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has NC: 2024:KHC-D:11488 rightly assessed monthly income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/- per month, which is just and proper and needs no interference.

He further submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in applying 15 as multiplier as the Aadhaar Card on record indicates that the the injured was aged about 41 years at the time of the accident.
He further submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal on all heads is just and proper, does not call for interference.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and meticulously perused the appeal papers along with material available on record.
7. The material available on record indicates that the appellant-claimant sustained grievous injuries in a road accident dated 31.05.2017.
The appellant sustained fracture of L-2 Vertebrae and other injuries.
Taking note of the same, the treated Doctor has assessed the disability at 20% to the whole body and considering the same, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 8%.

Taking note of the oral testimony of PW2 and other medical evidence available on record, I am of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:11488 considered view that it would be just and proper to re-assess disability at 10%
for the purpose of determination of compensation.

Admittedly, the appellant has not placed any cogent and acceptable evidence with regard to his income, hence, I am of the considered view that it Smt. Mallavva W/O Fakirappa Naykar vs The Depot Manager on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65381477/
2 would be just and appropriate to re-assess the income of the claimant notionally relying on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, relying on the above said chart, it would be appropriate to reassess the notional income of the claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month as the accident is of the year 2017.
8. The Tribunal has committed an error in applying 15 as multiplier as the Aadhaar Card on record indicates that the injured was aged about 41 years at the time of the accident.
Hence, appropriate multiplier would be 14.

Thus, loss of future income due to disability is recomputed as under:
Rs.10,250 (income) x 12(months) x 14(multiplier) x 10% (disability) = Rs.1,72,200/-
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11488

Taking note of the oral testimony of PW2 and other evidence available on record, this Court re-assesses the compensation as under:
 HEADS AMOUNT  (in Rs.)
Towards pain and suffering 30,000/-
Towards Medical expenses 24,821/-
Diet, nourishment, conveyance and 15,000/-
attendant charges Loss of income during laid-up period 30,750/-
(Rs.10,250 X 3 months)
Loss of future earnings due to disability 1,72,200/-
Loss of amenities 30,000/-

Thus, the claimant shall be entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,02,771/- as against Rs.1,77,121/-
awarded by the learned Tribunal.

10. In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant would be entitled to total compensation NC: 2024:KHC-D:11488 of Rs.3,02,771/- as against Rs.1,77,121/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till Smt. Mallavva W/O Fakirappa Naykar vs The Depot Manager on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65381477/
3 the date of payment.
d) The respondent-Corporation shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
e) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the appellant/claimant.
f) Registry to transmit the records, if any, forthwith to the Tribunal.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.

Sd/-
